headline: UK and EU agree trade deal; Burnham sees up to 17bn pounds a year
pages: Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the UK will explore even closer ties with the EU after the two sides agreed a deal in Brussels on Friday. It scraps most checks on British food exports in return for the UK following some EU rules from 2028, and covers emissions trading and a youth experience scheme. Burnham called it a good day for Britain and Europe, and said the Treasury believes it could boost the economy by up to 17 billion pounds a year. Legislation is expected in Parliament next week. Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said the deal is not fair, and Nigel Farage called it a betrayal.

BBC economics editor Faisal Islam noted that supermarkets welcomed the deal but have not promised lower prices. A separate plan to cut tuition fees for EU students was not agreed. Why it matters: it eases trade friction for exporters, though shoppers may not see lower bills. Source: BBC.
